comment.narrative: Georgianlanguage version of the EU organic regulation Report from a joint workshop with MEPA officials at which the regulation was brought to attention of the government and discussed

The European Union issued a new organic legislation applicable from 1 January 2022. The rules reflect the changing nature of this rapidly growing sector. The new regulation is designed to ensure fair competition for farmers whilst preventing fraud and maintaining consumer trust through the following production rules are simplified the control system is strengthened producers in third countries will have to comply with the same set of rules as those producing in the EU organic rules cover a wider list of products certification will be easier for small farmers thanks to a new system of group certification there will be a more uniform approach to reducing the risk of accidental contamination from pesticides.Translated regulations was shared with MEPA officials.The purpose of the roundtable was to inform major players in the organic sector about the ongoing and planned activities of GRETA project secure their support and active involvement in the upcoming Equivalency Assessment.The purpose of the Equivalency Assessment was to identify noncompliances and gaps analysing the pros and cons of its harmonization and compliance with the new EU organic regulations and provide recommendations if its approximation and continued equivalence under the Deep and Comprehensive Free Trade Area DCFTA is feasible.
